questions.q: According to Avogadro's Law, what happens to the volume of a flexible container if the number of moles of gas inside is doubled (at constant T and P)?
options: The volume increases by a factor of 4.
questions.explain: Avogadro's Law states that volume is directly proportional to the number of moles ($V \propto n$). Therefore, doubling the moles doubles the volume.

questions.q: What is the standard molar volume of an ideal gas at STP (Standard Temperature and Pressure, defined here as $0^\circ\text{C}$ and $1\ \text{atm}$)?
questions.explain: At STP ($0^\circ\text{C}$ and $1\ \text{atm}$), 1 mole of an ideal gas occupies approximately $22.4\ \text{L}$.

questions.q: Two balloons at the same temperature and pressure contain equal volumes of gas. Balloon A contains Helium (He) and Balloon B contains Argon (Ar). Which statement is true?
options: Balloon B has more atoms than Balloon A.
Balloon B has a greater mass than Balloon A.
Balloon A has higher kinetic energy than Balloon B.
The atoms in Balloon B are moving faster than in Balloon A.
questions.explain: Avogadro's Law implies equal volumes contain equal numbers of moles (and atoms for monoatomic gases). Since both have the same number of moles, the one with the higher molar mass (Argon, ~40 g/mol vs Helium, ~4 g/mol) will have a greater total mass.
